details:
@swirls/cli@0.1.148 ships no CLI implementation: the npm tarball contains only package.json, README.md, a 1.1KB placeholder bin/swirls stub, and scripts/install.js. The package's `postinstall` hook (`node scripts/install.js`) executes on every global install and fetches an unpinned remote installer outside the npm registry, piping it straight into a shell with the installer's full environment inherited: - Linux/macOS: execSync(`curl -fsSL hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install | bash`, { stdio: 'inherit', shell: true })
- Windows: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command `irm hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install[.]ps1 | iex`, with SWIRLS_YES=1 set in the child environment The script skips execution when CI=true/1 or when neither npm_config_global nor BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL is set. Nothing fetched is verified — no hash, signature or version pin is applied — so the code that actually runs at install time is whatever the remote endpoint serves at that moment. After the fetch-and-execute, the hook copies the downloaded binary from ~/.local/bin/swirls over bin/swirls and chmods it 0755, so every later `swirls` invocation runs the remote-downloaded file instead of the published package contents. The placeholder bin/swirls and bin/README.txt both direct the user to re-run the same `curl -fsSL hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install | bash` if the postinstall was skipped. The shipped JavaScript contains no credential, token,.env or.npmrc access; the only environment variables read are CI, npm_config_global, BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL, HOME and USERPROFILE, used for install-flow control. IOCs: hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install; hxxps://swirls[.]ai/install[.]ps1; dropped/copied file ~/.local/bin/swirls (installed mode 0755, then copied to node_modules/@swirls/cli/bin/swirls).
